stop_status: CLEAR after repair. The shared failed-initialisation class is closed crate-wide: every WPACKET_init_* entry point now writes `subs` on every return path, so cleanup after a refusal is defined. One pre-existing memory-safety defect (B23-D2, an out-of-bounds pointer formed by put_value after its final write) was found by the Miri run and repaired. No ABI, #[repr(C)] layout, exported symbol/signature, allocator seam or unsafe lint attribute changed; no hidden obligation remains.

authority.abi: No export, signature, #[repr(C)] layout or unsafe lint attribute changed. Wpacket/WpacketSub field order and widths are untouched; the CRYPTO_zalloc/CRYPTO_free seam coordinates (FILE_PACKET, LINE) are untouched. The only production additions are writes to an internal `subs` field, a guarded cursor decrement in a private fn, and `#[cfg(test)]` fault injection.
external_contracts: A WPACKET_init_* caller supplies a live `pkt` and, for the buffer-backed forms, a buffer writable for `len` bytes that outlives the packet. The authority rejects a NULL buffer or zero length before touching the packet.

After any WPACKET_init_* return, `subs` is written: an owned node on success, NULL on refusal. WPACKET_cleanup may therefore be called unconditionally after an init refusal, which is what the provider call sites do.
Only `subs` is guaranteed written when the argument guard refuses. No other field may be read after that refusal; the allocation-failure arm writes every field.
WPACKET_cleanup reads only `subs`; it is idempotent because it leaves `subs` NULL.

boundaries.mechanism: failed-initialisation state of wpacket_intern_init_len and every public WPACKET_init_* entry point, consumed by WPACKET_cleanup
boundaries.contract: wpacket_intern_init_len writes curr=0, written=0 and subs=NULL before the WPACKET_SUB allocation, mirroring the authority's direct `pkt->subs = OPENSSL_zalloc(...)` assignment (which leaves NULL on failure). It installs the node on success and leaves NULL on every failure. Each argument-refusal guard in WPACKET_init_static_len, WPACKET_init_der and WPACKET_init_len also writes subs=NULL before returning 0, so every init entry point writes subs on every path. WPACKET_cleanup requires subs to be NULL or the head of a chain this unit owns, reads nothing else, and leaves subs NULL. The task packet reserves nothing and does not expose a secret.

put_value is a private safe fn reached only from WPACKET_put_bytes__ and wpacket_intern_close, both of which pass a span established writable for `len` bytes (the reserved sub-packet length field or a WPACKET_allocate_bytes span). NULL `data` is the sizing pass and the authority's success. The walk stops after the final (first) byte, so no pointer one before the span is ever formed; the byte sequence written is unchanged.

defects.description: wpacket_intern_init_len wrote curr and written, then allocated the first WPACKET_SUB with `let Some(subs) = ... else { return 0 }`. On allocation failure it returned without ever writing pkt->subs, so a caller that cleaned up unconditionally read an uninitialised pointer and could free it. The authority writes `pkt->subs = OPENSSL_zalloc(...)` directly and therefore leaves NULL on the same failure. The class covered ecdsa_sig, dsa_sig, eddsa_sig, ml_dsa_sig, ml_kem_kmgmt, kdf (:2114-2150 and :4905-4923), and was worked around locally in slh_dsa_sig/sm2_sig by zeroing the packet (M70-D1).
defects.fix: src/packet.rs: `(*pkt).subs = core::ptr::null_mut()` before the OwnedSub::zalloc call, and the same write in the argument-refusal guards of WPACKET_init_static_len, WPACKET_init_der and WPACKET_init_len. The safety docs now state the cleanable failure state at every init entry point and at WPACKET_cleanup. The SLH-DSA and SM2 zeroing workarounds were reverted to the common MaybeUninit shape.

defects.description: put_value walked the cursor down after every write, including after the final (first) byte, forming `data - 1` one before the span. Miri (both Stacked and Tree Borrows) reported `in-bounds pointer arithmetic failed: attempting to offset pointer by -1 bytes ... at the beginning of the allocation` on the existing BUF_MEM round-trip test. The authority's `data--` has the same C UB; the Rust translation must not reproduce it.
defects.fix: The decrement is guarded by `if len > 0`, so the last write leaves the cursor at the first byte and no out-of-span pointer is formed. The bytes written are unchanged. This was discovered by the B23 Miri run, not introduced by the failed-init repair.

controls_observed: a_failed_sub_alloc_leaves_a_fully_initialised_cleanable_packet forces the next WPACKET_SUB allocation to fail through a #[cfg(test)] thread-local hook, starts from MaybeUninit::<Wpacket>, asserts init returns 0, reads every field (buf, staticbuf, maxsize, endfirst, curr, written, subs), asserts subs is NULL, then calls WPACKET_cleanup. Under Miri an uninitialised field is an error; under the normal harness a regression to an uninitialised read is exercised.

a_failed_sub_alloc_overwrites_a_poisoned_subs_field pre-fills the whole packet with 0xAA, forces the same failure, and asserts subs is NULL before cleanup. This is the deterministic negative control: if the root fix regresses and the failure path leaves subs untouched, the assertion fires with 'failed init left `subs` untouched (poisoned with 0xAA); cleanup would free it' before any garbage pointer is released.
The existing provider::slh_dsa_sig::tests::a_refused_der_init_leaves_a_cleanable_packet now exercises the argument-refusal arm at the call site; it passes.
Miri exposed B23-D2 in the existing a_buf_mem_backed_packet_round_trips_its_bytes test before the fix; the same test passes after the guarded decrement, which is the observed before/after witness.

safe_callers_can_cause_ub_note: Every WPACKET entry point is an unsafe fn / unsafe extern "C" with a stated contract; put_value is private and its only callers establish the writable span. No safe wrapper was added, and the failpoint cannot exist in a release build.

residuals.description: After an argument-guard refusal (NULL buffer or zero length), only `subs` is guaranteed written. A caller must not read buf/staticbuf/maxsize/endfirst/curr/written after that refusal; only WPACKET_cleanup is defined. No in-crate caller takes that path: every provider site passes a non-NULL buffer of non-zero length, so its refusal is the allocation-failure arm, which writes every field.

The init functions remain unsafe: `pkt` liveness and the buffer's writable extent/lifetime are caller obligations. The new failure-state guarantee is an implementer guarantee, not a removal of those obligations.

One threaded full-suite run on the final blob failed 17 secure-heap tests (CRYPTO_secure_malloc_init returned 0 after a reset that could not tear down a heap with live allocations); the immediate rerun of the identical suite passed 1676/0/27. No packet or provider-signature code is reachable from those tests. It is a process-global test-fixture ordering issue and needs its own investigation; it was not modified in this batch.

SAFETY_DISCHARGED applies to the two named mechanism scopes (failed-init state and put_value), not to the whole of packet.rs and not to any consumer family. No consumer becomes SAFE_COMPATIBLE from this receipt.

The pinned openssl-3.6.4 tree is not present in this checkout, so no byte-level authority diff or executable differential was run. The transcript claims rely on the authority source line references above.
